A.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume, $\rho = m/V$, and needs only magnitude with unit $\text{kg m}^{-3}$ - it is a scalar.

B.explanation: Mass measures amount of matter and needs only magnitude with unit $\text{kg}$ - it is a scalar.

C.explanation: Volume measures amount of space occupied and needs only magnitude with unit $\text{m}^3$ - it is a scalar.

D.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force $W = mg$ acting vertically downward with unit $\text{N}$ - it has magnitude and direction so is a vector.

hints: Notice the question asks for a vector, so check which of density, mass, volume and weight needs a direction as well as a magnitude.
Recall the link $W = mg$ where $g$ is gravitational field strength acting toward the centre of the Earth.
Compare mass, which only says how much matter there is, with the gravitational force on that mass - ask which one must point downward like other forces.
walkthrough: List what is given: four quantities - density, mass, volume and weight - and recall the test is whether magnitude alone is enough.
State the rule: a scalar has magnitude only, while a vector has both magnitude and direction.
Check density, mass and volume: $\rho = m/V$ in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, $m$ in $\text{kg}$, and $V$ in $\text{m}^3$ are all fully described by a number and unit with no direction.
Analyse weight: weight is a gravitational force given by $W = mg$, so it has magnitude in $\text{N}$ and a defined direction - vertically downward.
Therefore only weight satisfies the vector definition. This is option D.
